title: Sign-in binds to one chain because the chain is part of the DID (did:pkh:eip155:chainId:address)
content:
## The chain is inside the identifier

Renown sign-in happens on **one chain**, Ethereum mainnet by default. This is not a configuration limitation that could be relaxed — the chain id is a component of the user's DID:

```
did:pkh:eip155:<chainId>:<address>
```

So the same wallet on a different chain produces a **different DID**, which is a different user, with different credentials. There is no notion of one identity spanning chains.

## The behavioural consequence

A wallet session arriving from another chain is **rejected**, not accepted as a second identity for the same person. Wallets are offered for the issuing chain only, so a user connected to another network is prompted to switch rather than being allowed to sign in and then failing later.

That rejection is the correct behaviour precisely because the alternative — accepting it — would silently create a second, unrelated account holding none of the first account's permissions or reputation. From the authorization system's point of view the two addresses are unrelated principals: document permission grants key on the verified address, so a grant made to the mainnet identity means nothing to the same wallet's identity on another chain.

## Why the DID carries the chain at all

`did:pkh` is a DID method that derives an identifier from an on-chain account, and an on-chain account is only meaningful relative to a chain. Encoding `eip155:<chainId>` makes the identifier globally unambiguous — two chains can host the same 20-byte address with entirely different histories behind it, and a reputation system that conflated them would be trivially spoofable.

The practical rule for operators: pick the issuing chain deliberately and do not change it, because changing it invalidates every existing user identity rather than migrating it.

_Source: apps/academy/docs/academy/03-Build/03-BuildingUserExperiences/07-Authorization/01-RenownAuthenticationFlow.md (Powerhouse v6.2.2-dev.45)._
description: The same wallet on another chain is a different user with different credentials; a wallet session from another chain is rejected rather than accepted as a second identity.
